label: paragraph_title
text: WUCHANG'S FATE.

label: text
text: Counter-Offensive By Wu Pei-fu?

label: text
text:
Fengtiên and Sun Chuẩn-fang
Inactive.

label: text
text: Wuchang's fate still remains in mystery. The latest report, coming from Chinese sources, is that the city is defended by about 5,000 men under several Allied commanders.

label: text
text: It was at first stated that the fall of Hanyang and Tortoise Hill would render Wuchang untenable. The claim is now made that when the northerners retreated they took with them the vital parts of the guns on Tortoise Hill so that the southerners have to bring up heavy artillery before they are again able to shell Wuchang. Perhaps the presence of foreign warships may have had a desul

label: text
text: Wu Pei-ful is calling frantically for reinforcements and for half a million dollars to be raised by Dr. Wellington Koo in Peking.

label: text
text: Admiral Tu Hsi-kwen, the acting Premier, is reported to have gone South to rally the Navy and to urge Marshal Sun Chuan-fang to take the field against the southerners.

label: text
text:
Southerners Hall.
Marshal Wu has now made a definite stand but the southerners are not moving away from the north bank of the Yangtse River. Wu Pei-fu hopes to form a base at a certain point, rush down new forces from subordinates further North, cling to Wuchang, and send a detachment to attack the Nationalist flank. The breathing space of the last few days has given him time to take stock and he is not eclipsed, as far as appearances go.

label: text
text: The Fengtien party, although making boastful promises of an offensive against Chang Kai-shek, are clearing to Peking and the immediate vicinity.

label: text
text: Except at one point in Kiangsi province where a subordinate engaged the southern vanguard and then retired, Marshal Sun Chuan-fang has not entered hostilities.

label: text
text: The Chinese still give prominence to a series of communiques from Sun Chuan-fang, frantically asking for peace.

label: text
text:
Riots Break Out.
Hankow, Sept. 12.
Wuchang is still holding out.
Reuter:

label: text
text: Serious intercommunal riots broke broke out yesterday owing to reports that Honan troops, defending Wuchang, were ill treating the Hupeh people inside city. More than a dozen Honan coolies were beaten to death by mobs in Hanyang and in the Hankow native city. There, has always been bitterest feeling between these sections. The Honanese having the upper hand during the Wu Pei-fu regime while now the situation has switched over, the Hupehites are exacting revenge.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: FENGTIEN COMPLEX

label: text
text: Whether or not Marshal Chang Tso-lin will despatch the Fengtien forces to the south for the purpose of assisting Marshal Wu Pei-fu's forces chiefly depends upon Marshal Sun Chuan-fang's attitude.

label: text
text: There is a divergence of opinion between the leaders of the Fengtian and Shantung factions regarding despatch of the reinforcements to the south.

label: text
text: In this connection it is learnt on good authority that though Marshal Sun Chuan-fang's attitude is still ambiguous, the leaders of the Shantung faction, including General Chang Tsung-chang, will decide upon their course of action, on the basis that, as General Sun has already despatched part of his troops to Kiangsi, he will eventually join forces against the Cantonese troops.

label: text
text: In the meantime, Marshal Chang Tso-lin and other leaders of the Fengtien faction, who are said to entertain apprehensions regarding the real intentions of Marshal Sun, hold the view that, though he has already despatched some of his troops to Klangsi, he may side with the Cantonese and co-operate with General Chang Kai-shek—"Tohc."

label: paragraph_title
text: THIEF STRUGGLES WITH WATCHMAN

label: text
text: STABBED IN THE ARM

label: text
text: A gold wrist watch valued at $85 was stolen from the residence of Mr. G. A. Lawrence, manager of Messrs. A. S. Watson and Company's North Point factory, at about 1 A'clock yesterday morning.

label: text
text: The thief entered the house by an open window and commenced in contact with a chest of drawers in the grandish from which he took the wrist watch.

label: text
text: Apparently he was disturbed in his work, as he ran down a staircase leading to the main gate of the factory, where he was intercepted by a Russian watchman on the premises. A struggle took place between the two men and the thief eventually freed himself by stabbing the watchman in the upper part of the left arm. The wound was not serious, but it disabled the watchman for the time being and made him release his captive.

label: text
text: A report was made to the police and attempts to trace the man have so far proved unsuccessful.

label: paragraph_title
text: LOADED, PISTOLS.

label: paragraph_title
text: ARRESTS AT DOUGLAS. WHARF.

label: paragraph_title
text: CASE ON THURSDAY.

label: text
text: Another remand was made at the Central Magistracy this morning in the case of two Chinese charged with unlawful possession of two automatic pistols, one revolver, and 43 rounds of ammunition.

label: text
text:
The men were arrested during a watch kept by Senior Revenue Officer Watt and a party on the Douglas wharf on Thursday morning. One of the men came in a sampan alongside the vessel on which he was employed (s.s. "Hai Hong") with a bundle containing the arms. The two pistols were fully loaded.
Whether the alleged attempt to bring the arms aboard was with a view to carrying out a piracy as is thought will be disclosed when the case will be heard on Thursday afternoon before two Magistrates.

label: text
text: Mr. T. B. Wilson, who was the Asst. Manager of the Admiral and Oriental line in Manila is passing through "Hong Kong to Yokohama to relieve Mr. F. W. Thompson of the Admiral line office there. Mr. M. Thompson, also connected with the same firm, is en route to Seattle on leave of absence. Mr. Thompson is accompanied by Mrs. Thompson. They are sailing this afternoon at 5 p.m. by the "President Grant."

label: text
text: General Sun Chuan-fang in the present fighting: While Hankow reports state that he has actually sent troops to the assistance of his old chief, Marshal Wu Pei-fu, there is nothing to show that he has departed from his announced intention of maintaining neutrality in the dispute.

label: text
text: "Sitting on the fence" is the local description of his attitude, "but it is admitted that he has mobilised his army and has an army of 40,000 men along the Kiangsi-Hunnan border, concentrated at Pingziang practically opposite Changsha. General Lu, Haiang-ting. Tupan of Chekiang, who will take command of General Sun's forces if he is swept into the war, is at Kiuiklang.

label: text
text: Continual troops movements are reported from different parts of the province and all available soldiers are being sent to Nanking, for despatch to the probable war front. It is reported in some circles that General Sun's plan is to strike at Changsha and cut the communications of the Cantonese army. Nothing definite, however, appears to have been done along these lines.

label: text
text: Agents of General Chang Kai-shek, the Cantonese leader, are unremitting in their efforts to induce General Sun to swing over to the south, and take a definite step to seal the bargain. This would mean attacking Marshal Wu Pei-fu, a thing he has refused to do. Nevertheless, the Southern agents are persistent in their efforts and it is reported that as direct agents of the south have failed, the local branch of the Knomintang have sent their own personal delegate to see General Sun.—"Shanghai Times."

label: paragraph_title
text: SUICIDE OF DUTCH MERCHANT.

label: text
text: BUSINESS WORRIES.

label: text
text: [From Our Own Correspondent]

label: text
text: The body of Mr. W. H. Dop, a well-known Dutch merchant in Singapore, was found hanging yesterday in the garage which he owned.

label: text
text: It is believed that he was depressed by Business worries.

label: text
text: [Mr. Wessel Hendrin Dop was born at Utrecht, Holland, on February 21, 1895. He was formerly connected with Boasson and Van Overzee, Singapore; and Wilson, Holgate (Far East), Ltd. He later became proprietor of W. H. Dop's Trading Concern, which represented over 50 manufacturers in Europe and proprietor of the Singapore Advertising Bureau. Mr. Dop had travelled extensively in various parts of the world.]

label: paragraph_title
text:
RAIN DAMAGE.
LANDLORDS OF ADJOINING PROPERTY.

label: text
text: SLIT IN COURT

label: text
text: Damage alleged to have been done to an adjoining house as a result of the demolition of a house at 102 Kremer Street formed the subject of a Summary Court claim this morning. Chak Hoking, the landlord of 104 Kremer Street, claiming from Wat Pat-u $45 for repairs which he stated, were rendered necessary by water percolating through from a retaining wall which had been damaged by the demolition.

label: text
text: Mr. E. S. C. Brown for the plaintiff, stated that the plaintiff asked the defendant to put in hand the necessary repairs and as the work was not completed with

label: text
text: The report on the piracy of a Socony motor-boat will be found on page 4.

label: text
text: in two months the plaintiff arranged for the work himself and was claiming for the amount spent.

label: text
text: Mr. L. D. Turner, for the defence, contended that no notice stating the amount of damage and asking for repairs to be put in hand had been received. The first the defendant had known of it was after the repairs had been effected.

label: text
text: The plaintiff, in evidence, stated that the notice with regard to the damage and asking for repairs had been sent to the Tak Loong firm with which defendant was connected.

label: text
text: Questioned by His Honour, plaintiff said that he did not know defendant and had not been in direct communication with him.

label: text
text: His Honour said he did not think it could be held that notice had been given defendant of the need of repairs.

label: text
text: It was further claimed for the defendant that repairs to the party wall had been put in hand by the defendant shortly after the demolition of the house. There was no evidence, it was claimed, to show that the repairs it was necessary to do then were of the same nature and of the same seriousness as the repairs which were alleged to have been put in hand by the plaintiff after the heavy rains. It was submitted that the defendant's liability in respect of the condition of the party wall was not continuous after the demolition of the house.

label: text
text: His Honour adjourned the case to hear further legal argument as to how the case was affected by the failure of the plaintiff to give notice of the need of repairs.

label: paragraph_title
text: DISHONEST COOLIE

label: paragraph_title
text: ROBBED HIS MASTER'S MONEY.

label: text
text: CAUGHT IN THE ACT.

label: text
text: A coolia in the employment of the Rev. H. S. F. Rossiter, of No. 12, Broadwood Road, was the defendant in a charge of theft of money from his master. The case was heard by Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning.

label: text
text: Complainant stated that he missed small sums of money from time to time and set a trap by leaving one dollar worth of five-cent pieces inside a purse in a chest of drawers in a room, the door of which was left open. He entered the bathroom and kept a watch on the other room by the aid of a looking glass. By the reflection of the glass he was enabled to see the defendant take the purse and empty the content's into his hand.

label: text
text: The defence was that complainant purposely wanted to trap him by leaving two coins on the ground, but he picked them up and placed them on the table.

label: text
text: "You are a shameless hiar as well as a robber of your employer," said His Worship in imposing sentence of six weeks' hard labour.

label: paragraph_title
text: OPIUM TRAFFIC.

label: paragraph_title
text: ANIMATED DEBATE AT GENEVA.

label: text
text: PERSIAN ALLEGATION

label: text
text: Geneva, Sept. 12.

label: text
text: The discussion in "Committee regarding approval of last year's Opium Convention developed into an animated debate.

label: text
text: The Italian member, who last year agreed to the draft Convention, now opposed it on various points on the ground that they were a retrogression compared with The Hague Convention of 1922 which, he contended, if properly applied would effectively combat opium smoking.

label: text
text: Lord Cecil disputed the contention, declaring that last year's Convention approached Italian conceptions.

label: text
text: Subsequently the Indian and Persian delegates collided. The latter accused India of sending opium into Persia.

label: text
text: The discussion closed with the adoption of the report. The Italian delegate abstained from voting.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: THE UNKNOWN PERSON AGAIN.

label: text
text: GIRL OFFENDER.

label: text
text: On being charged at the Central Magistracy this morning with being found in possession of a quantity of illicit opium, a small Chinese girl pleaded that she was promised 25 cents by a man for carrying it.

label: text
text: It was shown that at the time of the discovery the girl was following her mother in the street, but the woman on being called up denied that she was aware of this.

label: text
text: In answer to the Magistrate, who pointed out that the fine in such cases would be $300 but in the present instance he would make it $100, the mother intimated that she was unable to pay on behalf of her daughter. The fine was allowed to stand.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: The British warship "Hawkins" flying the flag of Vice-Admiral Sir Edwin Alexander Sinclair (as Commander-in-Chief, China Station), on board which is H.R.H. Sub-Lt. Prince George, has arrived at Hankow and already its presence has had a moderating effect on the tension of the last few days. Sir Edwin is at once opening negotiations with General Yang Sen.—British Wireless Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: BRITISH NAVY'S REPLY:

label: paragraph_title
text: Chinese Headquarters Destroyed: 2,000 Casualties.

label: text
text: Hankow, Sept. 12.

label: text
text: An eyewitness's account of the Wanhsien's affair shows that at 5.50 in the afternoon on September 5, the U.S. Kiawo, man-ned by a naval detachment, went alongside the steamer "Wanhsien." All seemed quiet, the only persons visible was a group of Chinese squatting on the deck;

label: text
text: but directly the boarding party got aboard several machine-guns poured in a leaden hail; Darley and Higgins being amongst the first to fall.

label: text
text: It is estimated that 400 soldiers were packed on the Wanhisen's deck. A hot interchange of fire was kept up for some time, the Kiawo finally drawing off, having in the meantime rescued the ship's officers.

label: text
text:
Chinese Guns Silenced.
- Meanwhile several thousand troops, kept up a terrific fire from both sides of the banks, but the Widgeon going inshore, did tremendous execution with her quickfrers while the Cockchafer's six inchers, allenced the enemy fieldguns and destroyed Yang Sen's headquarters and other marked positions.

label: text
text: A conservative "estimate" places the Chinese casualties in the neighbourhood of 2,000 and in view of the tremendous odds the British casualties are extremely small. The engagement lasted one hour.

label: text
text: It was discovered afterwards that Yang Sen had decamped twenty miles inland, at two o'clock in the afternoon. It is reported to day that the foreigners on the Wanhsien are safe aboard a Japanese gunboat.—Reuter.

label: text
text: "Kiawo" Attacked Again. Hankow, September 10.

label: text
text:
Firing on foreign steamers continues. The latest incident is Butterfield and Swire's S.S. Wuchang and the Japanese S.S. Yoyang; though fortunately there were no casualties.
The S.S. Kiawo, from Ichang, bearing the naval officers and men wounded at the Wanhsien affair, was heavily fired on when passing Hanyang last night and was forced to turn back up the river. This morning another attempt was made but the fusillade was so severe that she again had to turn back.

label: text
text: The naval wounded were taken off by an American destroyer this morning; while this afternoon H.M.S. Cricket proceeded up the river and escorted the Kiawo to safety.—Reuter.

label: text
text: Further "Bee" Details.

label: text
text: Hankow, September 9.—Yesterday H.M.S. Bee returning from the A.P.C. installation, where she was taking/on fuel, was deliberately shelled by the southerners near Luchlamiao. In all six shells were fired one striking the armour plating diagonally and glancing into the water; fortunately not exploding, otherwise the consequences would have been serious.

label: text
text: The Bee did not return the fire but slewed a gun towards the shore observing which the soldiers retreated.—Reuter.
